quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn to let the cyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bike lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the cyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as you can. Cyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too fast can force them off course.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in an accident because they are small.
Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanation: Children who are too small for regular seat belts need special child seats. No adult is strong enough to hold a child safely during an accident or sudden stop. Always use a proper seat for children.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and others is important because it:

options.text: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
Keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Extra space gives you time to react to mistakes by other drivers.

questions.question: You must pull over to the edge of the road for an emergency vehicle:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is behind you or coming toward you.

questions.question: At a flashing red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Stop only if other cars are in the intersection.
Slow down and stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop, let traffic pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, you should:

options.text: Have your exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.
Keep your engine off when your car is in an enclosed garage.
Close vents when driving behind another car.

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is odorless and deadly. Signs include sudden tiredness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. Fresh air is the only cure.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows that control turns from certain lanes. A green arrow:

options.text: Is only used on one-way streets.
Works like a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
Only works if there is also a circular green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Works like a green light, but you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you have a green light. You must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: The Implied Consent Law means:

options.text: Someone has permission to drive your vehicle.
Drivers agree to a breath test if arrested for drinking and driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers agree to a breath test if arrested for drinking and driving.
questions.explanation: The Implied Consent Law means that by driving on the road, you consent to a breath test if arrested for an alcohol-related offense.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up. Turn on your signal, look for an opening, and match the speed of other traffic. Then merge safely into that opening.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how fast you drink, and your weight. Food slows alcohol absorption but does not stop intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same as:
questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop completely and let all other traffic pass first.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit show?

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed in all road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed in good road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest legal speed for that road. However, you may need to drive slower than the limit depending on conditions. Always slow down when roads are wet, icy, or crowded.

questions.question: How can you avoid alcohol-related car crashes?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Simply refuse a drink by saying you are driving.

questions.explanation: Plan not to drive before you drink. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after drinking has started.

questions.question: How does distraction affect driving?

options.text: It usually slows how fast the driver reacts to hazards.
It usually makes the driver go faster.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: It usually slows how fast the driver reacts to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react slower to traffic and road hazards. Distracted driving is always unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver behind you wants to pass?

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slowing down creates space in front of your car. This lets the other driver pass more easily and quickly.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and roadsides continuously.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and roadsides continuously.
questions.explanation: Find problems before you reach them. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look ahead and scan the sides of the road too.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a divider between them. You must stay on the right side.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is available.
If no right lane exists, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This encourages the tailgater to pass you.

questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you and there is a right lane, move to it. If there is no right lane, slow down gradually when the road ahead is clear. This lets the tailgater pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights and/or siren, you must drive to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: What can you do to avoid emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance between your car and the one in front.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than the traffic flow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance between your car and the one in front.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems ahead without emergency braking. This protects the driver behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: Night driving requires extra caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it harder to see. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may only cross a solid yellow line when turning.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for an hour or more.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads become very slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain because water brings oil to the road surface. This is worse in hot weather, when heat increases the amount of oil that rises.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers know in advance that you plan to pass.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or around a curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, before railroad crossings, on bridges, or in any no-passing zone. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights.

questions.question: What happens if a bicyclist breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Bicyclists do not have to obey traffic laws.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights, duties, and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can be ticketed for breaking traffic laws.

questions.question: When must you turn on your headlights?

options.text: When stopped at a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: Use headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, when using windshield wipers, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Auxiliary lights cannot replace headlights.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or slippery. Driving too fast on poor roads makes it hard to control your vehicle and stop safely.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging into traffic is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Always check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors, as they cannot see everything.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop at an unmarked railroad crossing. Look both ways on all tracks for approaching trains. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until the train passes before crossing.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Do not pass in tunnels, on bridges, or in underpasses. Only pass where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: When driving through an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross.
They will stop at the curb.
They will run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross without an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus on driving. Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile driven. Any extra activity, even small ones, can be dangerous and cause accidents.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance work. Slow down and drive carefully when you see this sign. Be ready for unusual or dangerous conditions in the work area.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts crossing in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front.

questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop for pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way in crosswalks.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Pass the animal as closely as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road onto the shoulder, what should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels go off the pavement, reduce your speed without hard braking. Carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for other traffic before returning to the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane. It warns you to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space between your car and the car ahead?
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your car when stopped going uphill. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic moves, there is less chance of a crash.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to stop.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.

questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings when a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices tell you to. Not all crossings have lights or gates. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: A driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that this driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving. If another driver seems distracted, stay farther away from them. A distracted driver is more likely to crash.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must carry your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your car when you drive. You must show all three when stopped by police.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your car?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on your speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: The faster you drive, the less grip your tires have.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
Slowing down makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster you drive, the less grip your tires have.
questions.explanation: When you drive fast on a wet road, your tires cannot push water away as well. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane (slide on water).

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of danger ahead. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: Keep your eyes on the road. Quickly shift into neutral and press the brake pedal firmly. Pull safely off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: A sign with this shape and color is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: This pennant-shaped sign means no passing zone. It is only used for this purpose.
